claims.text: Increasing batch size may enable capture, but can delay the first response and increase unnecessary I/O when clients do not consume all results. (low confidence)
Enable profiling through a custom cluster parameter group and separately enable the cluster's profiler log export; configuring only one side does not deliver logs. (high confidence)

AWS documents query-log coverage only when the entire result fits in one batch and remains under 16 MB. Increasing batch size can improve capture but delay the first response and waste I/O when results are discarded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Pabis demonstrates a low-traffic DocumentDB 4.0 test with a 50 ms threshold, sampling 1.0, and Terraform-enabled profiler exports. AWS recommends starting with a high threshold and lowering it gradually; it warns that 50 ms can cause performance issues for high-throughput applications, so the Pabis configuration should not be treated as a general default for those workloads. (low confidence)
Amazon DocumentDB's profiler captures slow database operations above a configured duration threshold and exports their execution details to CloudWatch Logs for investigation. (high confidence)

Plan summaries such as COLLSCAN help connect slow operations to missing indexes. One independent production account used profiler evidence to identify scan-heavy upserts and verify that those entries disappeared after indexing. (high confidence)
Profiler delivery is best effort, and sampling can omit eligible slow operations. Absence from CloudWatch Logs therefore cannot establish that an operation was fast. (low confidence)

An October 2022 user report described missing slow aggregate pipelines containing $lookup while other slow operations were logged. The thread provides no confirmed cause or general proof that $lookup is unsupported. (low confidence)
The profiler records slow-operation duration and command details in CloudWatch Logs; logged evidence can include planSummary and client metadata. (high confidence)
AWS documents a default 100 ms threshold, a 50 ms minimum, and a default sampling fraction of 1.0; sampling applies to slow operations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

AWS documents best-effort delivery and requires the complete query result to fit one batch and remain under 16 MB for slow-query logging. Missing entries therefore do not prove fast execution. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

In an August 2026 production account, Castañeda used slow upsert COLLSCAN records to select indexes, then reported that those slow entries stopped appearing. This is a single incident, not a general performance guarantee. (low confidence)
The profiler applies across all databases and instances in a cluster. Its records include command, duration, plan summary and client metadata. (low confidence)
CloudWatch stores profiler output under /aws/docdb/<cluster-name>/profiler, with instance-specific streams; Logs Insights can filter and rank the resulting operations. (high confidence)
Profiling consumes cluster resources. Start with a higher duration threshold and lower it deliberately; low thresholds on busy clusters can increase overhead and log volume. (high confidence)

A November 2021 Terraform AWS provider 3.61.0 issue reported recurring profiler_sampling_rate plan differences between values '1' and '1.0'. This is historical provider behavior, not evidence of a current DocumentDB profiling defect. (low confidence)
Profiling applies across all databases and instances in the cluster. (low confidence)
COLLSCAN profiler entries can identify missing indexes in update/upsert paths, not only read queries. (high confidence)

Castañeda reports that attaching a new parameter group required instance restarts in his environment; parameter-group attachment should be evaluated separately from changing an already-active profiler parameter. (low confidence)
